# Original sample deliveries

These five files preserve the exact bytes of the original delivered samples.
They are additions, not replacements for the compact fixtures in the parent
folder. The MIT license in `../LICENSE` applies to these synthetic datasets.

| File | Original content |
| --- | --- |
| `terrain-4096.las` | 4,096 LAS 1.4 points with RGB/GPS and EPSG:32632. |
| `streaming-16384.copc.laz` | 16,384 real compressed points, 132 chunks and 9 hierarchy pages. |
| `ordinary-original.tiff` | Original 512 x 512 RGB TIFF, without geographic tags. |
| `geotiff-striped-original.tif` | Original striped GeoTIFF with EPSG:32632. |
| `imagery-overviews-original.cog.tif` | Original COG with overview factors 2, 4 and 8. |

`manifest.json` records byte sizes, SHA-256 hashes and Git blob identities.
The parent fixture manifest includes every original binary as well.

From the repository root, with the pinned fixture Python dependencies installed:

```sh
python packages/renderers/3d/scripts/restore-geo3d-originals.py \
  --output packages/renderers/3d/test/fixtures/geo3d/samples-mit/original-deliveries \
  --verify-only
```

Omit `--verify-only` to regenerate missing original files. The command first
checks generated bytes against fixed original hashes, never rewrites compact
fixtures, and refuses to replace different existing data. It also decodes all
COPC records, checks raster pixels/CRS/overviews and exercises real HTTP ranges.

Restoration on the repository runner matched the delivered bytes exactly.
The large COPC range check decoded 429 points using six HTTP 206 responses,
transferring 5,371 of 145,393 bytes, without a complete-file request. These are
fixture/transport checks, not a performance benchmark for production datasets.
